text: September payrolls badly missed at just 29,000 jobs while inflation reaccelerated to 3.7% with the Fed signaling another possible rate hike — this stagflationary mix (slowing growth plus rising prices) means you should be cautious about adding new risk right now.
Sell QBTS — it's down 64% and nearly 73% off its high with no earnings, burning cash, and heavy short selling, meaning other investors are actively betting against it; there's no reason to hold this.

Sell IONQ — down 43% with deeply negative earnings, insiders are selling their own shares, and 12% of the stock is being shorted; the quantum computing thesis hasn't translated into real business results.
Sell RGTI — down 62% with revenue actually shrinking, 21% short interest (meaning one in five available shares is bet against it), and insiders dumping stock; this is a broken position.
Trim MSTR — it's 51% off its high with terrible cash flow of negative 41% and insiders selling, and as a Bitcoin proxy it adds extra volatility you don't need in a stagflationary environment.
Trim BMNR — three straight earnings misses, down nearly 58% from its high with weak momentum; the company keeps disappointing and the stock reflects that.
Consider adding to ADBE — at a price-to-earnings ratio of just 9.2 with strong cash flow and steady 10.5% revenue growth, Adobe looks genuinely cheap for a high-quality software company.
Consider adding to MU — a PE of 4 with 256% revenue growth is extraordinary value, and the consensus view on Wall Street remains positive despite the broader market weakness.
